company_summary: Harbor & Pine Goods is a two-person studio in Portland making small-batch linen and ceramics. Wholesale opened this year, and the founders still answer every shop themselves.
pain_points: Wholesale orders are tracked in a spreadsheet, so availability lives in a file instead of in the reply to the shop.
Shops still reorder by email, and the same thread has to carry stock, terms, and the ship date.
Two founders answering the inbox can disagree with the sheet about what is actually on the shelf.
ai_opportunities: A reorder note could show what the sheet says is in stock, so the founder is not retyping the same check.
Terms and the ship date could be filled from the last confirmed order instead of copied between threads.
A weekly diff of the sheet against open email would catch a reply that promises stock the studio no longer has.
value_proposition: The useful conversation is which part of an order a shop could confirm without another email, and which part should stay a personal note from the studio.
recommended_angle: Wholesale orders tracked in a spreadsheet while shops still reorder by email.
